stories.headline: AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models
stories.summary: When Keelan Miskell began winding down his crypto startup this year, he didn’t think its data was worth much: the users were anonymous, the company just a few years old. But he’s since turned the firm’s digital archives into real money.
stories.why_it_matters: He’s netted roughly $25,000 for his code base and a still-pending amount (likely around $15,000) for the workspace data in Google, Notion, Figma, and Slack. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in ai & machine learning.

stories.headline: Martin Shkreli livestreamed himself violating lifetime pharma ban, FTC says
stories.summary: Martin Shkreli—the ex-pharmaceutical executive infamous for illegally hiking the price of a lifesaving anti-parasitic drug by more than 4,000 percent and getting a seven-year prison sentence for the fraudulent scheme he used to do it— has been under a lifetime ban from the pharmaceutical industry since 2022. However, according to the Federal Trade Commission and the attorneys general of seven states, Shkreli has "flagrantly and repeatedly" violated that ban nearly the entire time—allegedly by trading stock in dozens of drug companies and discussing the industry during livestreams on social media.
stories.why_it_matters: On Tuesday, the FTC and the seven states asked a federal judge to hold Shkreli in contempt for the alleged violations. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in developers.

stories.headline: ESA targets Anbernic emulation handhelds as "superfake" piracy enablers
stories.summary: For years, Chinese hardware manufacturers have carved out a market niche with an array of handheld Android gaming devices focused on retro emulation and/or more modern game-streaming capabilities. Now, though, a major game industry trade group is targeting one of those manufacturers, Anbernic, asking the US Trade Representative (USTR) to add the company to its list of "Notorious Markets" that "engage in or facilitate substantial copyright piracy or trademark counterfeiting." TorrentFreak was among the first to notice the request from the Entertainment Software Association (ESA), which was submitted to the USTR last week.
stories.why_it_matters: In it, the US trade group—which represents major publishers including Nintendo, Microsoft, PlayStation, Amazon, Epic, EA, Ubisoft, and more —notes that Anbernic devices "are routinely offered or shipped with removable memory cards preloaded with hundreds or thousands of unauthorized copies of copyright-protected video games published by ESA members." While many online sellers do include an SD card full of ROMs alongside emulation hardware of all types, Anbernic itself does not appear to do the same when selling directly from its website. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in developers.

stories.headline: Anthropic Warns Small AI Models Could Soon Form Self-Propagating IoT Botnets
stories.summary: Small artificial intelligence (AI) models may be months away from developing capabilities to self-replicate on IoT devices like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes, according to a warning from Anthropic. The frontier AI lab said small AI models could form autonomous, self-propagating worm botnets that are "challenging to shut down," since "there's no centralized point to shut off.".

stories.headline: Docker Fixes Critical Two-Year-Old Hub Flaw That Let One User Push Images as Another
stories.summary: A flaw in Docker Hub, the registry where container images are published and downloaded, let one user push, pull, or delete images as another user. Docker fixed the flaw on September 30 and says it found no evidence that anyone exploited it.
stories.why_it_matters: The flaw was in the feature that converts a personal account into an organization, Docker said in a security advisory on October 12. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in cybersecurity.

stories.headline: CISA director touts private partnerships after agency killed many
stories.summary: The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has killed many of the industry partnerships it used to enhance security, but don't tell the organization's acting director. Speaking on Tuesday at a virtual public sector cyber resilience summit hosted by infosec firm Rubrik, Nick Andersen claimed that CISA’s public-private partnerships are the most critical aspect of his agency’s mission.
stories.why_it_matters: We’re not a law enforcement agency, intelligence agency, or a regulator,” Andersen said during a discussion at the summit. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in cloud.
key_points: Problem & Context: The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has killed many of the industry partnerships it used to enhance security, but don't tell the organization's acting director.

Technical Implementation: CISA’s mission simply can’t succeed without motivating those various partners to share what they’ve seen, heard, and dealt with in order to build a comprehensive threat model.

Deployment & Impact: “It’s all carrots and partnerships,” Andersen added, referring to motivating partners to get on board with programs like CISA’s CI Fortify initiative for building resilient critical infrastructure.

stories.headline: Announcing AWS Lambda Web Functions
stories.summary: Today, we’re announcing AWS Lambda Web Functions , a new form factor that lets you run standard HTTP web applications on Lambda without rewriting your code into an event handler. You can take a standard port-listening server built with Express, Hono, Fastify, Next.js, or any Node.js framework, deploy it with a single command, and Lambda automatically handles scaling, multi-region distribution, and active CPU billing.
stories.why_it_matters: No adapters, no infrastructure to manage, and no framework lock-in. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in cloud.
key_points: Problem & Context: Today, we’re announcing AWS Lambda Web Functions , a new form factor that lets you run standard HTTP web applications on Lambda without rewriting your code into an event handler.
Technical Implementation: With this launch, AWS Lambda now offers three distinct form factors, each built on the same Firecracker isolation technology and designed for a different programming model.
Deployment & Impact: They use the event-driven, single-concurrent handler model with wall-clock billing.
